title: Register for Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis in Children in Germany (LCH REG DE 2025)
summary:
Since Langerhanscell-Histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare disease overall, international collaboration is underway to jointly analyze data on its incidence and course, thereby laying the groundwork for a better understanding of the disease as well as improved diagnosis and treatment. The registry is intended to help better document not only the frequency of individual subtypes but also their respective courses; however, the registry does not influence your child’s treatment. 
The responsibility for and decision regarding treatment lies with the treating physician for each patient and is completely independent of this registry. 
Where possible, all consenting patients (ages 0–18) with LCH in Germany should participate in the registry.

Objectives of Our Registry
Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare disease overall; it is sometimes diagnosed incidentally (e.g., in patients with asymptomatic bone findings), but it can also cause life-threatening, severe clinical presentations. In some patients, the disease resolves without treatment, while others require intensive care. 

Therefore, there are many questions we hope to answer with this registry. 

1)    Epidemiology in Germany
In recent years, a comparison of data from various registries has shown that only a portion of patients with LCH are currently recorded. The new registry is intended to uniformly record all patients, thereby enabling the determination of the exact number of affected patients, along with their age and disease patterns, for Germany.
2)	Treatment and Prognosis
Although first-line therapy is well established, the treatment and prognosis for relapses—particularly multiple relapses—remain relatively unclear. Additionally, the use of new classes of drugs, such as MAP kinase inhibitors, is increasing. Here, the registry aims to provide evidence-based data and identify patients who could benefit from participating in clinical trials. 
3)	The registry will focus particularly on neurodegenerative LCH (ND-LCH), a condition that affects only a small number of patients. Data on risk factors, diagnostic procedures, and therapy will be collected to provide better treatment for these patients in the future. 
4)	Future research questions should also address quality of life both during the acute phase of the disease and in the long term. To this end, questionnaires on so-called “patient-reported outcomes” will be integrated into the registry in the future
conditions: Multifocal and multisystemic (disseminated) Langerhans-cell histiocytosis [Letterer-Siwe disease]

interventions.name: Survey on epidemiological data, clinical presentations, disease progression, follow-up care, and complications associated with the disease. The data are collected prospectively.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The cohort is defined as follows:
•    Patients with histologically confirmed Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH)
•    Exception: Patients with diabetes insipidus not caused by a germ cell tumor (“strong suspicion of LCH”); this specific patient population may be included in the registry despite the lack of histological confirmation of LCH  
The following inclusion criteria are defined:
•    Age 0–18 years  
•    Consent from legal guardians and patients (as appropriate for age) is available
Exclusion criteria:
The following exclusion criteria have been defined:
•    Age >18 years at initial enrollment
•    No histological confirmation of LCH (exception: diabetes insipidus of unknown cause; see above)
•    No written informed consent on file
